title: Psychological Predictors of Risky Sexual Behaviors in Nursing Students: A Multivariate Analysis
content: Objective: To determine the predictive value of emotional intelligence, anxiety, academic stress, and impulsivity on risk sexual behaviors in Nursing students. Methodology: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 257 Mexican nursing students. Validated instruments were applied, and hierarchical multiple linear regression was performed, controlling for sociodemographic variables. Results: The final model explained 19.3% of the variance in risk sexual behaviors. Age (β = .170, p = .008) and academic stress (β = .246, p = .002) were the only significant predictors. Emotional intelligence, anxiety, and impulsivity did not show independent predictive capacity. Conclusions: Academic stress is the main psychological predictor of risk sexual behaviors. Interventions should prioritize stress management and emotional regulation over exclusive information provision, integrating mental health as central to promoting healthy sexual behaviors.
